reference_role: The supplied gameplay screenshot is a style reference only; the two existing shops are rejected temporary reskins.
clockmaker: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original game building design sheet for Haverlund, a gently fantastical seaside town of painted 3D limestone, plaster, timber and tiled roofs with fine dark outlines. Design a wholly original CLOCKMAKER shop, Pendulum & Pin, not a recolored ordinary townhouse. It must be a compact shop building with a memorable architectural silhouette: a narrow two-storey workshop anchored by an offset square clock turret, an exposed readable pendulum behind a tall glazed bay, a deep recessed entrance and broad ground-floor watch/clock display windows facing the shopping promenade. Restrained patinated copper roof details and honey oak joinery, pale weathered limestone lower walls, warm plaster above. Integrate the clock into the architecture; modest brass mechanical details with plausible supports, no giant loose decorative gears. The facade and entrance must read at a small orthographic gameplay scale. Buildable human-scale geometry, a clear level ground threshold, blank side party wall suitable beside future shops, and a considered rear with a small workroom window rather than a featureless box. Composition: one polished concept sheet, large front-right three-quarter orthographic-like view and a smaller consistent rear-left view of this SAME building on warm ivory paper, both fully visible roof to foundations, no cropped edges. Painterly architectural game concept, crisp forms and restrained surface detail, grounded cozy fantasy rather than photorealism, not low-poly voxel blocks. Show a tiny plain unlabelled human silhouette for scale if needed. Small paving apron only, no street scene, no other buildings, no interiors, no UI, no technical diagram. Readable fascia text PENDULUM & PIN only, no additional captions or watermark. This is a unique original building; avoid the standard orange-roofed gabled townhouse with two sash windows and a stock shopfront from the reference.
apothecary: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original game building design sheet for Haverlund, a gently fantastical seaside town of painted 3D limestone, plaster, timber and tiled roofs with fine dark outlines. Design a wholly original APOTHECARY shop, Thyme & Tonic, clearly different in shape and construction from a clockmaker tower and from a standard seaside townhouse. Low, broad, asymmetrical one-and-a-half-storey herb shop: a rounded or faceted glazed corner shopfront with a sheltered recessed entrance, a lower attached herb-growing glasshouse/sunroom as part of the building, and a steep short slate-green roof over the main room. Pale limewashed masonry, dark aged green timber, weathered limestone plinth, a little muted plum on a door or shutter. A wrought-iron mortar-and-pestle hanging sign, a few orderly amber/green labelled bottle silhouettes visible behind glass, restrained herb window boxes and an exterior herb drying rail. No bubble foliage; use simple readable leaf sprigs. The entrance and glazing must read clearly at small orthographic gameplay scale. Plausible buildable geometry and supports, level doorstep, a finished rear with a small service door and herb glasshouse rather than blank walls. Composition: one polished concept sheet, large front-right three-quarter orthographic-like view and a smaller consistent rear-left view of the SAME building on warm ivory paper, fully visible roof to foundations with margin. Painterly architectural game concept, crisp forms and restrained detail, grounded cozy fantasy rather than photorealism, not low-poly voxel blocks. Small paving apron only, no town scene, no other buildings, no interiors, no UI, no technical diagram. Readable fascia text THYME & TONIC only, no extra captions or watermark. Avoid a recolored ordinary orange-roofed two-storey gabled shop-house; this should feel designed for a herbalist from the foundations up.
